Interoperable Europe Act

Regulation (EU) 2024/903 laying down measures for a high level of public sector interoperability across the Union (Interoperable Europe Act)

Official text: Regulation (EU) 2024/903 of 13 March 2024 laying down measures for a high level of public sector interoperability across the Union (Interoperable Europe Act) (OJ L 2024/903, 22.3.2024)Tier 1 · primary law

Status
Applicable as of 28 October 2026
Key dates
3 dated events
Competent authority
not established in this dataset
Sanction ceiling
no amount recorded

In force since 11 April 2024, the twentieth day after publication (Art. 23(1); OJ L 2024/903, 22.3.2024). It applies from 12 July 2024, and its interoperability assessment (Art. 3(1)–(4)) and the rules on national competent authorities and single points of contact (Art. 17) from 12 January 2025 (Art. 23(2)); both dates have passed. Read on 28 Oct 2026 in the Official Journal text retrieved from the Publications Office's Cellar; the Publications Office's metadata records it in force, with the same three dates.

In short: what you need to know

  • Objective: Common rules and a governance framework that promote the cross-border interoperability of trans-European digital public services, and so of the network and information systems beneath them, for the Union entities and public sector bodies that regulate, provide, manage or implement those services.
  • Who it binds: Union entity · Public sector body · Member State
  • Who it protects: not established
  • Core obligations: Interoperable Europe Act Art. 3 · Interoperable Europe Act Art. 4 key provisions →
  • Key dates: Entry into force 11 April 2024 · Application date 12 July 2024 · Application date 12 January 2025 the timeline →
  • Sanction ceiling: no amount recordedNone: no Article of the Regulation sets fines or penalties (the Official Journal text, read in full on 28 Oct 2026). Recital 41 recalls that the European Data Protection Supervisor may impose administrative fines on Union entities in the interoperability regulatory sandboxes under Art. 58(2)(i) of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725. enforcement →

What does the Interoperable Europe Act do?

Common rules and a governance framework that promote the cross-border interoperability of trans-European digital public services, and so of the network and information systems beneath them, for the Union entities and public sector bodies that regulate, provide, manage or implement those services.

When does the Interoperable Europe Act apply? Key dates

Entry into force, application and transposition are different events and are kept apart. A date at month precision is shown as a month rather than invented as a day.

  1. 11 April 2024Entry into forceEntry into force
  2. 12 July 2024Application dateThe Regulation applies (Art. 23(2), first subparagraph), except Article 3(1) to (4) and Article 17, which apply from 12 January 2025.
  3. 12 January 2025Application dateThe interoperability assessment (Article 3(1) to (4)) and the designation of national competent authorities and single points of contact (Article 17) apply (Art. 23(2), second subparagraph). Article 3(5), on the Board's guidelines, applies from the general date.

What does the Interoperable Europe Act require? Key provisions

4 provisions recorded. This is what the dataset holds, not the whole instrument — an article that is not here has not been entered, which is a different statement from its not existing.

ArticleHeadingBindsApplies
Art. 3 load-bearingInteroperability assessmentBefore taking a decision on new or substantially modified binding requirements, a Union entity or public sector body carries out an interoperability assessment; none is needed where one has already been carried out for those requirements or where they are implemented by solutions provided by Union entities (3(1)). The assessment identifies the effects of the requirements on cross-border interoperability, the stakeholders concerned and the Interoperable Europe solutions that support their implementation, and a report on its outcome, covering the items in the Annex, is published on an official website and shared with the Interoperable Europe Board (3(2)). The recipients of the services directly affected, including citizens, are consulted (3(4)).Union entity · Public sector bodyApplies from 12 January 2025 a date set for named provisions: what it covers is under Key dates →
Art. 4 load-bearingShare and reuse of interoperability solutions between Union entities and public sector bodiesA Union entity or public sector body makes an interoperability solution supporting a trans-European digital public service, with its technical documentation and, where applicable, its documented source code, available to any other Union entity or public sector body that requests it (4(1)). The obligation does not cover solutions supporting processes outside the entity's public task, solutions for which third parties hold restricting intellectual property rights, or solutions excluded on grounds of critical infrastructure protection, defence or public security (4(1)(a)–(c)). Publishing on the Interoperable Europe portal fulfils it (4(3)). Solutions without restrictive licensing terms, such as open source solutions, are prioritised where they are equivalent (4(6)).Union entity · Public sector bodyApplies from 12 July 2024 the instrument’s general date; nothing specific to this article is recorded
Art. 17National competent authorities and single points of contactEach Member State designates one or more competent authorities responsible for the application of the Regulation, and a single point of contact from among them (17(1)), with the coordination and support tasks listed in 17(2). Member States ensure the authorities have adequate competence and resources (17(3)), notify the Commission of the single point of contact and make its designation public (17(5)).Member StateApplies from 12 January 2025 a date set for named provisions: what it covers is under Key dates →
Art. 18Interoperability coordinators for Union entitiesAny Union entity that regulates, provides or manages trans-European digital public services designates an interoperability coordinator, under the oversight of its highest level of management, who supports that entity in setting up or adapting its internal processes to implement the interoperability assessment.Union entityApplies from 12 July 2024 the instrument’s general date; nothing specific to this article is recorded

How does the Interoperable Europe Act interact with other EU laws?

2 recorded interactions with other instruments — each with a direction, the provisions that carry it and its own sources. Direction is preserved as recorded: an instrument that amends another is not the same as one amended by it.

Interoperable Europe Act Defers to GDPR

This instrument leaves a matter to the other: a without-prejudice clause, a 'shall not affect' clause or an express reference sending the reader there. The locator is in the DEFERRING instrument's text (from). Added 27 Oct 2026 (docs/V2-DATA-DESIGN.md §1.4).

A consultation on an interoperability regulatory sandbox does not replace the GDPR's prior consultation, and processing in a sandbox leaves the data subjects' GDPR rights unaffected.

NIS2 Enables Interoperable Europe Act

The other instrument's provisions operate through definitions, bodies, means or populations this instrument establishes, and say so. Recorded only on an express reference in the DEPENDENT instrument's text; the locator is in that text. Direction: from = the enabling instrument. Added 27 Oct 2026 (docs/V2-DATA-DESIGN.md §1.4).

The Interoperable Europe Act defines the network and information systems whose interoperability it promotes by reference to NIS2.
